title: Change an H4 headlamp bulb from behind the lamp: tabs into notches by eye, glass untouched, then hook its wire clip
instruction: Fit the new headlamp bulb from the holder into the headlamp and secure it with the wire clip. Hold the bulb by its base only.
context: Automotive service technicians and mechanics (O*NET 49-3023; roughly 0.8 million US jobs, approximate figure) replace headlamp bulbs at routine service and inspection. H4 (P43t) halogen bulbs are a common headlamp type, and in lamps of this style a U-shaped wire spring clip holds the bulb. The bulb's reference flange has three unequal tabs that fit the lamp's notches one way only; the robot must judge the turn from the tab and notch patterns it sees. A tab left on the rim leaves the bulb proud and loose and the beam aimed wrong. The glass must not be touched (skin oil shortens halogen life), and the clip must be pushed past its catch's spring. Plug and dust boot are already off.
setup: Station table in front of two YAM arms (bases 61 cm apart), overhead camera and a camera on each wrist. Positions in cm: x forward from the line between the arm bases, y to the robot's left of their midpoint. (1) Rear of a 7 in round H4 headlamp (dark grey back shell 178 mm) mounted in an engine-bay mock-up: bulb bore axis horizontal at x 40, y 0, 15 cm above the table, the bulb goes in along +x (away from the robot). The bulb boss: 20.6 mm bore (0.8 mm lead-in), a locating rim (37.8 mm bore with a 0.8 mm x 45 deg lead-in, 1.0 mm high) with three notches for the bulb's tabs (seen from the robot: one wide at the top, two narrow ones low on the right and lower left, at 250 and 335 deg from the robot's left measured over the top). A U-shaped 1.6 mm spring-wire clip is hinged on a vertical axis 26 mm to the robot's left of the bore; its legs cross the flange 15 mm above and below the axis and its end hooks under a sprung plastic catch 26 mm to the right of the bore. It starts swung open toward the robot by 95 to 105 deg. Around the lamp: a radiator support panel (50 x 30 cm) ahead, a battery box (16 x 16 x 10 cm) to the left rear at x 30, y 20 and the inner fender apron (18 x 2 x 11 cm) to the right at x 32, y -16.5. (2) New H4 halogen bulb (12 V 60/55 W, P43t-38 cap, e.g. Philips 12342; 18 g) standing glass down in an orange foam holder at x 21.5, y -6 (moved up to 1 cm in x and y per trial): the flange rests on the holder's 32 mm rim, the cap and its three blades up; its roll in the holder (tab pattern) is drawn per trial uniformly over 360 deg. Plug and dust boot are off. Named check setups: rolls 37, -124, 151, -58, 92 deg with clip angles 104, 100, 96, 102, 98 deg, holder not moved (real trials use these, set from 1 deg angle scales printed on the holder rim and the lamp shell).
scoring: Read at the end of the trial (person check in brackets). 0 if at any time the robot touched the glass envelope (video; in sim any contact force between a robot link and the glass) or the bulb was dropped (video; sim: falling faster than 0.3 m/s with no robot contact). Seated = the flange flush in the rim all round and the bulb cannot be turned (sim: flange front face within 0.4 mm of the seat, tilt < 1 deg, roll within 4 deg of the fitted roll, only possible with all three tabs in their notches). 0.25: seated, clip open. 0.5: seated and the clip swung over the flange but not hooked under the catch (a light pull on the clip end frees it; sim: bail within 6 deg of closed), or hooked with a hand still within 3 cm of the bulb or the clip. 1.0 (ends the trial): seated, clip hooked under its catch (a light pull does not free it; sim: bail within 1.2 deg of closed, catch back over the wire), both hands 3 cm or more from the bulb and the clip, bulb still for 1 s. Otherwise 0 (bulb in the holder, in a hand, cocked on a tab or out).
reset_notes: Press the catch aside, swing the clip open to the next setup's angle (1 deg scale on the lamp shell), take the bulb out by its cap (gloves) and stand it glass down in the holder turned to the next setup's roll (1 deg scale on the holder rim). Setups run in order 0-4.
fidelity: Isaac Lab-Arena yam_arena, PhysX (CPU) 480 Hz, 20 Hz control, full size. Bulb dimensions representative (cap drawing not available); glass is a separate collider. Lamp, bay and holder kinematic; bay parts lowered for reach. Clip: rigid wire bail on a hinge (mass raised, speed cap); bending preload not modelled. Catch: sprung slide (4 N + 1.6 N/mm, est.) for the wire's sideways spring. No welds or snaps. Full statement: README.
run_limit: 2400 control steps (2 min at 20 Hz). The trial also ends as soon as the score reaches 1.0.
scores: Dream-1: 0.0 (seed 0, 2,400 steps). Scripted demo: 1.0 in the official Inspect Robots run (default seed, 1,220 steps); 1.0 twice, identical, direct; 1.0 at seed 7. Doing nothing: 0. Fixed grasp angle: 0. Demo replayed open-loop at seed 7: 0.
